summary: Added POST /abort_request to the Rust sgl-router. The route forwards the original body and safe transport headers to every registered plain or prefill/decode worker with bounded concurrency, reports per-worker outcomes, and returns 502 for partial or total upstream failure. The unmodified native router returned 404; the rebuilt patched router returned 200 and the recording worker received the exact payload and Authorization header.

tests.command: cargo build (Rust 1.90, unmodified base) followed by curl POST http://127.0.0.1:49125/abort_request
tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before reproduction against the actual base binary: the router returned HTTP 404. Raw evidence: /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-8025dbc2aede/evidence/base-cargo-build.log, base-abort-status.txt, base-abort-headers.txt, and base-abort-body.txt.

Eight focused native Rust tests covering successful fleet fan-out, exact body and Authorization forwarding, forward-compatible unknown fields, opaque malformed input delegated to workers, partial 422 failure, unreachable workers, empty registries, trailing-slash URLs, and both prefill/decode modes. tests.command: rebuilt sgl-router plus recording HTTP worker; curl POST /abort_request with Authorization and a future field
tests.what_was_measured: Passing-after black-box transport: router returned HTTP 200 with a one-worker success result; worker received /abort_request, the byte-equivalent JSON payload including the unknown future field, and Bearer transport-test. Raw evidence: /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-8025dbc2aede/evidence/patched-router.log, fake-worker.log, patched-abort-status.txt, patched-abort-headers.txt, and patched-abort-body.txt.

remaining_limitations: No weighted model or distributed inference workload was run. The native router transport was validated with a recording HTTP worker; worker-side abort semantics remain covered by SGLang's existing engine tests rather than requalified here.
The router intentionally broadcasts because it has no durable request-owner mapping. This is correct for SGLang's unknown-rid no-op contract but costs one bounded HTTP request per registered worker.
A strict cargo clippy -- -D warnings gate is currently blocked by an unrelated pre-existing warning at experimental/sgl-router/src/policies/buckets.rs:167.
